messages.subject: Resolving error in script from AHM book
parts:
Dear All,

I am working through the Kery & Royle's AHM book, with the script they provide online (relevant sections posted below). I have been running the models in Chapter 11, but when I get to model 6 I get into the following; "Error in mcmc.list(x) : Different start, end or thin values in each chain". 

I am using the MHB dataset that comes with the AHMbook package, and haven't changed any part of the script. I was wondering if anyone else had run into this issue? I have updated R and all packages to the most recent versions, I have started from scratch with a clean environment. The error message appears even when I use a thin value of 1.

Apologies in advance, I must be doing something daft, but I can't figure it out. Any help or pointers would be really appreciated.

Kind regards,
Tom


library(AHMbook)
library(jagsUI)

## Data preparation and exploration in Chapter 11.
# Section 11.3, p 643 - 646. Taken from the AHM book script, lines 10422 - 10472.

# Code modified to use the built-in data set MHB2014 instead of the file "MHB_2014.csv"
data(MHB2014)
?MHB2014
str(MHB2014)

# Check the detection data in 3D array
( nsite <- nrow(MHB2014$sites) )    # number of sites in Swiss MHB = 267
nrep <- 3             # maximum number of replicate surveys per season
( nspec <- nrow(MHB2014$species) )  # 158 species occur in the 2014 data
dim(MHB2014$count) == c(nsite, nrep, nspec) # check

# Convert the counts array to the detection/nondetection (1/0) array
y <- MHB2014$count
y[y > 1] <- 1  ## 'Y' replaced with 'y'
str(y)

# Check data for one species, here chaffinch, and pull them out from 3D array
head(tmp <- y[, , "Common Chaffinch"])

# Frequency distribution of number of surveys actually carried out per site in 2014
# NB MHB2014$sites$nsurvey gives the number of surveys *planned*, so need to follow this instead.
table(nsurveys <- apply(!is.na(y[,,1]), 1, sum)) # 0 = 1,  2 = 47,  3 = 219

# Which site has all NA data in 2014 ? Q030 was not surveyed in 2014
(NAsites <- which(nsurveys == 0) )

# Number of occupied sites for each species
tmp <- apply(y, c(1,3), max, na.rm = TRUE)
# For the 'all NA' site, max returns -Inf with a warning
tmp[tmp == -Inf] <- NA         # Change -Inf to NA
sort(obs.occ <- apply(tmp, 2, sum, na.rm = TRUE))


# Plot species 'occurrence frequency' distribution
plot(sort(obs.occ), xlab = "Species number", ylab = "Number of quads with detections")

# Drop data from species that were not observed in 2014
toss.out <- which(obs.occ == 0) # 13 species
y <- y[,,-toss.out] # Remove those 13 from y
obs.occ <- obs.occ[-toss.out] # Remove those 13 from the number of occupied sites

# Redefine nspec as the number of species observed in 2014: 145
( nspec <- dim(y)[3] )

# Check y. 3D array with 267 sites (chr), 3 reps (chr), and 145 species (chr) 
str(y)

# Get number of species observed per site
tmp <- apply(y, c(1,3), max, na.rm = TRUE)
tmp[tmp == "-Inf"] <- NA
sort(C <- apply(tmp, 1, sum)) # Compute and print sorted species counts per site

# Plot with mean value highlighted
plot(table(C), xlim = c(0, 60), xlab = "Observed number of species", ylab = "Number of quadrats", frame = FALSE)
abline(v = mean(C, na.rm = TRUE), col = "blue", lwd = 3)



# Section 11.6.1, p 663. Taken from the AHM book script, lines 10773 - 10775.
# Collapse 3D detection/nondetection data to 2D detection frequencies
ysum <- apply(y, c(1,3), sum, na.rm = T) 
str(ysum) # sites as rows (chr), species as columns (chr)
ysum[NAsites,] <- NA # Have to NA out sites with NA data



# Section 11.6.2, p 668 - 671. Taken from the AHM book script, lines 10859 - 10926.

# Bundle data into a list for the model
str( win.data <- list(ysum = ysum, M = nrow(ysum), J = MHB2014$sites$nsurvey, nspec = dim(ysum)[2], R = matrix(c(5,0,0,1), ncol = 2), df = 3) )

# Specify model in BUGS language
sink("model6.txt")
cat("
    model {
    
    # Priors
    for(k in 1:nspec){  # Group lpsi and lp together in array eta
    lpsi[k] <- eta[k,1]
    lp[k] <- eta[k,2]
    eta[k, 1:2] ~ dmnorm(mu.eta[], Omega[,])
    }
    # Hyperpriors
    # Priors for mu.lpsi=mu.eta[1] and mu.lp=mu.eta[2]
    # probs = community means of occupancy and detection probability
    for(v in 1:2){
    mu.eta[v] <- log(probs[v] / (1-probs[v]))
    probs[v] ~ dunif(0,1)
    }
    # Prior for variance-covariance matrix
    Omega[1:2, 1:2] ~ dwish(R[,], df)
    Sigma[1:2, 1:2] <- inverse(Omega[,])
    
    # Ecological model for latent occurrence z (process model)
    for(k in 1:nspec){
    logit(psi[k]) <- lpsi[k]   # Must take outside of i loop
    for (i in 1:M) {
    z[i,k] ~ dbern(psi[k])
    }
    }
    
    # Observation model for observed data y
    for(k in 1:nspec){
    logit(p[k]) <- lp[k]       # Needs to be outside of i loop
    for (i in 1:M) {
    mu.p[i,k] <- z[i,k] * p[k]
    ysum[i,k] ~ dbin(mu.p[i,k], J[i])
    }
    }
    
    # Derived quantities
    rho <- Sigma[1,2] / sqrt(Sigma[1,1] * Sigma[2,2])  # Correlation coefficient
    for(k in 1:nspec){
    Nocc.fs[k] <- sum(z[,k])   # Number of occupied sites among the 267
    }
    for (i in 1:M) {
    Nsite[i] <- sum(z[i,])     # Number of occurring species
    }
    }
    ",fill = TRUE)
sink()


# Initial values to give the model a starting point.
zst <- apply(y, c(1,3), max) # Observed occurrence as starting values for z. Equivalent to ysum, but for presence/absence only across all surveys.
zst[is.na(zst)] <- 1 # One site with missing data, replace NAs with 1. Don't know why.
# Define function for use in the model. Omega and eta are parameters in the model.
inits <- function() list(z = zst, Omega = matrix(c(1,0,0,1), ncol = 2), eta = matrix(0, nrow = nspec, ncol = 2))

# Parameters monitored, output desired from the model.
params <- c("mu.eta", "probs", "psi", "p", "Nsite", "Nocc.fs", "Sigma", "rho")

# MCMC settings
ni <- 20000   ;   nt <- 15   ;   nb <- 5000   ;   nc <- 3

# Call JAGS from R
out6 <- jags(win.data, inits, params, "model6.txt", n.chains = nc, n.thin = nt, n.iter = ni, n.burnin = nb, parallel = TRUE)

# Returns "Error in mcmc.list(x) : Different start, end or thin values in each chain"

parts:
Hi Tom,

I've not really figured out exactly why this error pops up (I'd be curious to hear some of the details, if anybody else knows--maybe Ken Kellner?), but I think it is has to do with ni not being divisible by nt (or at least, making ni divisible by nt has seemed to fix this error most or maybe all of the time for me).

Cheers,

John

messages.author: 983257fd4b8064bd
messages.subject: Re: Resolving error in script from AHM book
parts:
Hi John,

Yes, that was my first thought when faced with the error. I've tried it with nt = 1, as I thought it would resolve the division issue, but still get the same error. It's weird, because I have been able to run that model in the past.

However, I've had a direct email from Nathan which has helped, here is his email;

Hi Tom,

This may be an issue with the adaptation phase. Try setting 'n.adapt = 1000' in the jags() function (it may need to be higher for this example). 

Discussion of this issue is on the unmarked google group page (here).

-Nathan


I hadn't thought to check the unmarked google group before. I set "n.adapt = 1000" as suggested and the model seems to be running ok now. From the discussion in that link, the explanation is "The issue seems to be the adaptation phase, which seems to end up taking a different number of iterations in the different chains, so when the output is combined the chains don't match in length."

Hopefully this will help anyone else who runs into the same. Thanks both John and Nathan!

Tom
